\label{lemma-diagonal-and-differentials}
Let $(A, I, \gamma) \to (B, J, \delta)$ be a homomorphism
of divided power rings. Let $(B(1), J(1), \delta(1))$ be the coproduct
of $(B, J, \delta)$ with itself over $(A, I, \gamma)$, i.e.,
such that
$$
\xymatrix{
(B, J, \delta) \ar[r] & (B(1), J(1), \delta(1)) \\
(A, I, \gamma) \ar[r] \ar[u] & (B, J, \delta) \ar[u]
}
$$
is cocartesian. Denote $K = \Ker(B(1) \to B)$.
Then $K \cap J(1) \subset J(1)$ is preserved by the divided power
structure and
$$
\Omega_{B/A, \delta} = K/ \left(K^2 + (K \cap J(1))^{[2]}\right)
$$
canonically.

final_content.statement:
A divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ is a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and operations $\gamma_n:I\to I$ ($n\ge1$), with $\gamma_0(x)=1$, $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_n(ax)=a^n\gamma_n(x)$, $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(x)\gamma_j(y)$, $\gamma_m(x)\gamma_n(x)=\binom{m+n}{m}\gamma_{m+n}(x)$, and $\gamma_m(\gamma_n(x))=(mn)!/(m!(n!)^m)\,\gamma_{mn}(x)$. A homomorphism of divided power rings carries distinguished ideals into one another and commutes with all divided power operations.

For a divided power ideal $(I,\gamma)$, $I^{[n]}$ is the ideal generated by products $\prod_j\gamma_{e_j}(x_j)$ with $x_j\in I$ and $\sum e_j\ge n$, with $I^{[0]}=A$ and $I^{[1]}=I$. The ideal $I^{[2]}$ consists of terms of divided-power order at least two.

Given a ring map $A\to B$ and a divided power ideal $(J,\delta)$ on $B$, a divided power $A$-derivation $d:B\to M$ into a $B$-module is additive, vanishes on $A$, satisfies $d(bb')=b\,d(b')+b'\,d(b)$, and $d(\delta_n(x))=\delta_{n-1}(x)d(x)$ for $x\in J$. The universal module representing such derivations is $\Omega_{B/A,\delta}$ with universal map $d_{B/A,\delta}$. The ordinary Kähler differential module $\Omega_{B/A}$ represents all $A$-derivations. For a divided power scheme $(T,\mathcal J,\delta)\to S$, the sheaf $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ represents divided power derivations and is the quotient of $\Omega_{T/S}$ by the divided-power derivative relations.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-module-differentials-divided-power-envelope}
Let $(A, I, \gamma)$ be a divided power ring. Let $A \to B$ be a ring
map and let $IB \subset J \subset B$ be an ideal. Let
$D_{B, \gamma}(J) = (D, \bar J, \bar \gamma)$ be the divided power envelope.
Then we have
$$
\Omega_{D/A, \bar\gamma} = \Omega_{B/A} \otimes_B D
$$
